finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts::hand-rolled `asciitrim` uses a quadratic backtracking trim regex on attacker-controllable note content (redos → preview/tab hang)
evidence: Verified at packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:19-23: the global regex `/^[\x09...\x20]+|[\x09...\x20]+$/g` has an unanchored trailing alternative, so `String.replace` retries `[ws]+$` at every offset and backtracks the whole run each time — the textbook quadratic trim (trim-newlines / CVE-2021-33623 shape); `^` without `m` makes the first alternative cheap, so it offers no protection. It is applied to `state.getLines(...)` in the lheading heading branch (reached by any `Text\n===`/`---` paragraph), and preview.ts's `md.render` is synchronous and re-run from editor.ts's `docChanged` updateListener, so a note containing a long internal whitespace run followed by non-whitespace freezes the tab on every edit or remote patch. I could not execute the code or inspect the installed markdown-it to confirm the secondary claim that upstream `lheading` uses native `.trim()`, but the quadratic pattern exists in this file as written. Severity is major rather than critical: it is a crafted-input, availability-only DoS requiring a very large whitespace run from a collaborator, not a data or integrity compromise.
